name: Tweezers For Extracting Hair
description: FROM CARD: "BRASS TWEEZERS HUNG TO A ROUND BEADED CORD. THIS SPECIMEN WAS PRESENTED BY PERRI PA HOU EE AN ARAPAHO CHIEF, TO DR. F. KAUFF [sic, should be Kampf] [Las] VEGAS, N.MEX. NOTE THE TENT DESIGN ON THE TWEEZERS." "Tent design" consists of two triangles with crosses on top. Possibly could also represent a mission/church? Original list in accession file identifies as "Brass tweezers for extracting the hair. Presented by Perri-Pa-hoo-ee, a Chief of the Arapahoes, to Dr. F. Kampf, at Las Vegas, New Mexico." Rau acquired the tweezers from Kampf. Dr. F. (Ferdinand) Kampf was a civilian astronomer on the Wheeler Survey, 1873 - 1878 (his last season in the field ended in 1877).

name: Knife Set "Kukri"
description: SHEATHED KNIFE W/ 2 ACCOMPANYING UTILITY KNIVES. DONOR'S REMARKS: "BURMESE KUCKREE...A RITUAL...AS DESCRIBED TO ME, WHEN A MALE CHILD REACHES THE PROPER AGE, HE MUST EARN THE RIGHT TO HIS KUCKREE-AN INVOLVED CEREMONY." FURTHER INDICATES THEY ARE WORN BY BURMESE TROOPS SERVING W/ BRITISH ARMED FORCES. GOOD CONDITION. name: Shell Scraper
description: Scraper made from a shell, cut into a square, and lashed to a folded, rough cloth, and used to remove outer layers from bast of paper mulberry. The scraper is part of a collection of kapa tools used to make barkcloth, and was made specifically for the U.S. Exploring Expedition conservation project that took place in the Department of Anthropology Conservation Lab at the Museum Support Center in 2012-2013. The scraper was made by Daniel Richard Jonathan Kapalikuokalani Maile of Kaimuki, Oahu, age 25, a Masters candidate at UH Manoa-Pacific Island Studies.
